content: {"rule": "K-G4", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The text counts verses carried in the D2 vs C3 clash (Matthew 1:18, 25, Luke 1:34) as the witnesses that break a side's link, which is the verse-counting this rule governs.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "D2 vs C3 (Matthew 1:18, 25): CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN -- [L1] Matthew 1:18 'before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost' and Matthew 1:25 'knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son' contradict C3's claim of espousal union; [L2] πρὶν ἢ συνελθεῖν (prin ē synelthein, Strong's G4250/G4905, before coming together) and οὐκ ἐγίνωσκεν (ouk eginōsken, Strong's G1097, was not knowing); [L3] Luke 1:34.", "rule_words": "A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count.", "room": "'counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round' — reading one: the LINK BROKEN verdict rests on the clash's cited verses standing against C3, so the judge had to quote the earlier round's pressing sentence and name that round; reading two: the judge is only offering its own fresh verse analysis (Greek glosses, an added Luke 1:34), which the rule does not reach; I weighed reading one because the verdict counts the debate's own clash verses, and no round sentence is quoted and no round is named anywhere in the text.", "why": "The judge breaks the link on the strength of cited verses while quoting no earlier round's sentence and naming no round, so under K-G4 those verses cannot count as unanswered witnesses, yet the break rests on counting them anyway."}
